ch1_intro.title: Earth is running out
ch1_intro.narrative: Pete Conrad believed anyone could reach the stars. He never got to see the Moon's ice. You will. But first — Earth. Three regions. Three crises. The same problem from different altitudes. The Conrad Council needs an answer in 72 hours. Choose where to start.

ch1_region_select.title: Where do you go first?
ch1_region_select.narrative: Three signals are flashing on the Mission Water board. Each region has a water emergency the Council can't ignore. You have one trip to spend. Pick the one that calls to you — every choice opens a different science.

choices.text: Mumbai — chemicals in the drinking water
São Paulo — three years without rain

ch1_phoenix_arrive.title: Phoenix — the Ogallala Aquifer
ch1_phoenix_arrive.narrative: The Ogallala Aquifer fed eight states for a century. Now the wells are pulling sand. Farmers stand at the edge of a field that hasn't grown in two seasons. A research team has a sensor rig you can deploy — but their hydrologist wants to talk first. What do you do?

choices.text: Deploy the sensor rig — measure the drawdown
Talk to the farmers first — hear the history

ch1_phoenix_findings.title: Phoenix — findings
ch1_phoenix_findings.narrative: The Ogallala loses 2.5 km³ a year. Recharge from rainfall is one-tenth of withdrawal. It took the aquifer 6,000 years to fill. It is emptying in 100. The number on your tablet says the same thing the farmer said: this place is on the clock. The Conrad Council is waiting.

choices.text: Report back to the Conrad Council

ch1_mumbai_arrive.title: Mumbai — chemicals in the water
ch1_mumbai_arrive.narrative: The drinking water in three districts tests positive for PFAS — "forever chemicals" that don't break down. A municipal lab has clean samples and a story; a community health team has bad samples and a wider story. Where do you spend the morning?

choices.text: Run the lab samples — find the source
Meet the health team — map the exposure

ch1_mumbai_findings.title: Mumbai — findings
ch1_mumbai_findings.narrative: PFAS readings in the affected districts are 14× the WHO safe limit. The molecules have carbon-fluorine bonds that don't decompose for thousands of years. The water plant strips bacteria, not chemistry. Mumbai needs a treatment system that doesn't exist yet at scale — or a different source. The Conrad Council needs to hear this.

choices.text: Report back to the Conrad Council

ch1_sao_paulo_arrive.title: São Paulo — three years without rain
ch1_sao_paulo_arrive.narrative: The Cantareira reservoir system is at 4% capacity. A La Niña pattern has held three years longer than any model predicted. A climatologist wants to show you the upstream data; a farmer wants to show you the downstream cost. You can do one before the council meets.

choices.text: Walk the farmland with the grower

ch1_sao_paulo_findings.title: São Paulo — findings
ch1_sao_paulo_findings.narrative: Atmospheric rivers that used to deliver moisture inland have shifted south by 400 km. The climate hasn't broken — it has moved. São Paulo's water system was built for a place that no longer exists at this latitude. Adaptation is no longer optional. The Conrad Council needs to hear this.

choices.text: Report back to the Conrad Council

ch1_council_reveal.title: The Conrad Council
ch1_council_reveal.narrative: You stand in front of the Conrad Council. The three crises overlay on the same screen: groundwater going, chemistry contaminating, climate moving. Nancy Conrad speaks first. "It is the same problem from three altitudes. We do not have new water on Earth. The water that exists is the water we have. So we look up." The lights dim. A new map appears. The Moon. Polar craters. Ice.

choices.text: Accept the mission to the Moon

ch1_end.title: End of Chapter 1
ch1_end.narrative: Earth is behind you. The journey begins. Chapter 2 — "The Journey to the Moon" — opens soon. Bring your discoveries.
